To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

repeated testing in mice results in contrasting behavioural responses and this is accompanied by strain-specific differences in c-Fos activity and CRFR1 and glutamaterg receptors in relevant brain areas.

repeated testing in a novel environment results in contrasting behavioural responses and c-Fos expression profiles in brain areas regulating cognition and emotion, and that this may be the result from a shift in the balance between glutamatergics, CRFR1 and CRFR2 expression.

repeated testing in mice with different habituation behaviour results in contrasting behavioural responses, which are accompanied by strain-specific changes in c-Fos activity and receptor mRNA-expression in brain areas regulating emotion and cognitive processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of habituation behaviour in mice, and may provide new insights into the neurobiology of anxiety and stress-related behaviour.
the identification of brain areas involved in the regulation between emotion processing and cognitive processing.
the neural basis of habituation behaviour in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-adaptable behaviour in 129P mice may be the result from an altered processing of emotional and cognitive information, possibly regulated by CRFR1 and/or mGlu5Rs.

the non-adaptation to a novel environment in 129P2/J mice, which is accompanied by a lack of habituation, is the result of a lack of a cognitive shift over time, which is reflected in the expression of c-Fos in brain areas regulating emotional and cognitive processes, as well as in CRFR1 and glutamate receptor mRNA expression in the prelimbic cortex and amygdaloid nuclei.
129P3 strain mice are less able to adapt to novel environments and this is reflected by a strain-specific expression of c-Fos and CRFR1 and/or mGlu5 mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the non-adapted behavioural response in 129P mice to a novel environmental stimulus is accompanied by a shift in neural activation in brain areas involved in cognitive processing and emotional responses.
repeated testing results in strain-specific behavioural responses that are accompanied by strain-specific alterations of c-Fos activity and receptor mRNA expression.
129P3 and BALB/c mice differ in their behavioural response to repeated testing in a novel environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 129P3 strain may represent a model for studying the neural basis for the development of maladaptive behaviour.

the non-adapted response of 129 mice is the result of impaired processing between the prelimubic cortex and brain areas regulating emotional processing, possibly mediated by glutamateric neurotransmission and the CRFR1 system.
repeated testing of 129P2 and BALB/c mice resulted in contrasting behavioural and molecular profiles.
